questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being close to nature and having opportunities to explore beautiful BC

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of it was pretty straightforward, they gave very useful information during the intro days on everything from the bus pass, how to get around uni, services that the uni offers etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The exchange office at Uvic was extremely helpful and would reply to emails very quickly, so I would definitely recommend reaching out to them about anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If you want to live off campus you definitely have to put in a bit more effort. I joined a bunch of Uvic off campus housing groups and would frequently write to people posting in the groups. It took quite a few messages before I got one, but for me it was worth it in the end. I would recommend starting the process early if you want to find off campus accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think there are pros and cons to both on campus and off campus. I chose off campus because I prefer not living in student dorms and having a bit more space/being in a more homey place. I lived only a 10 min bike ride to campus, so I was extremely lucky, but if you want to be closer to everyone else doing exchange then on campus would be the better choice. For me I enjoyed being able to leave uni to separate uni from my everyday life. I would definitely not recommend living too far from uni because then you can miss some of the more spontaneous social things on campus. I also preferred living in a house off campus because I wanted roommates who were a bit older/more mature who took care of our home. Quite a few of my friends who lived with very young people on campus didn't know how to clean and they were quite frustrated with that. So it completely depends on what you prioritise.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration process where you had to log in at a specific time was a bit confusing for me because there were some subjects that didnt match in the registration, and it was a bit stressful to try and get all the subjects I got the pre approval for. However, I thought it was nice that you could see the times of the classes so you can make your own schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange office was quite helpful, so I would recommend just reaching out to them whenever you have a question. The emails they sent out about the deadlines were also useful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end I got some of the classes I wanted, so overall I was happy. I definitely dont think you can expect to get all the classes you want, so just be prepared for that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have all the pre approval stuff ready and do some research on each of the classes before you sign up. Communicate with the Uvic exchange team if you are confused about anything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The classes I took were pretty manageable, but there are a lot more deadlines than at UCPH. In a way I enjoyed that because it meant that there wasn't one big exam at the end of the semester, but that it was spread out. Some courses I took were very Canada focused, so of course that took some getting used to and I had to learn quite a lot about BC and local policy, but I found that very interesting. The grading wasn't so harsh, at least not in the classes I took.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different, at UCPH I only have big lecture style classes, whereas at Uvic it was mostly smaller tutorial style classes. It definitely took me out of my comfort zone, but in a good way. I felt that I learnt a lot more by participating in my classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Environmental Impact Assessment, Public Policy Process, Issues in Politics: Memory and Democracy & Foundations for Program Evaluation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Issues in Politics: Memory and Democracy, because it was a unique course and we had an amazing teacher who pushed us to think critically and gain new perspectives on how we view democracy and what we can learn from the past.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My unexpected costs were the clubs I joined and the gym (which I hadn't accounted for), and definitely also all the trips that I went on. It was hard to know before you go how much you are going to spend on trips, but you end up spending quite a lot especially since you have to drive a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were very expensive, and also renting cars.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have clubs for everything and for anyone. Personally I joined the outdoor club and the rowing club. I went on an amazing 4 day hike with the outdoor club, and it was planned really well and I had a great time. Once you are a member you can also borrow any of their outdoor gear throughout the semester, which was amazing, so you can go on our own trips. Definitely join as much as you can!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anything outdoors, go hiking, biking, swimming and explore as much of the beautiful nature as you can.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Vancouver Island is one of the most beautiful places I have ever been, so I recommend driving around the island and exploring as much as you can there. My favourite places on the island are: Tofino, Ucluelet, Lake Cowichan, skiing on Mount Washington, East Sooke regional park, Botanical Beach, Port Renfrew, Qualicum Beach. Definitely go explore the surrounding islands as well, unfortunately I only had time to visit Salt Spring Island but that was really cool. Off the island, I would definitely recommend hiking the Sunshine Coast trail on mainland BC, and visiting Banff national park and Jasper national park in Alberta. I took a weekend trip to Vancouver, but to be honest that was not a highlight for me. The best places were out in nature exploring the beautiful scenery that BC has to offer. I would also really recommend doing whale watching, surfing, skiing, paddleboarding, camping and generally just any fun outdoor activity!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, people are extremely friendly and extroverted.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just say hi to everyone in your classes, people are very friendly and open to get to know you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The car culture, even though Victoria is known to be one of the most bike friendly cities in Canada, it doesn't compare to cph of course. I had a bike but it was very far to go to the city center and generally there were quite a lot of roads I didnt feel comfortable biking on because there weren't any bike lanes. Also the unhealthy eating culture, it was quite hard to find actual organic food and healthy food options.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendly culture, everyone was extremely open and always wanted to talk and help and learn about your culture. Very opposite of Danish culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make the most out of the days you have there, time goes by really quickly. Put yourself out there, meet as many people as you can, and dont be afraid to ask people in the beginning if they want to go on a trip, they are new too. Remember that exams are not the end of the world, you will get through them all and pass, so don't say no to any fun trips because you are stressed.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much beforehand, everything will work out!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the amazing people I met that turned into friends, and all the amazing trips we took together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not much, maybe just the occasional stress of practical things and uni

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Make sure you have a credit card with you so you can rent a car!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
